parts:
Hello MSStats Team,

I am relatively new to MSStats and MSStatsTMT, so I am not completely sure, whether I understand the capabilities correctly.

I have the following dataset: 

samples from 11 patients' tumors were collected. Primary tumour and later the recurrent tumor specimen again. So I have a total of 22 samples from 11 individuals.

These 22 samples were distributed over 3 TMT Experiments, always evenly dividing primary and recurring tumor. So Exp1 consists of 4 primary and 4 recurring etc.

Additionally, 2 Mastermix Channels were included in every TMT Experiment. Experiments were fractionated before measurement.

1. Can MSStatsTMT analyze such a dataset?

2. I now have 10 channels in Exp1 and Exp2, but only 8 in Exp3 and MSStatsTMT gives me the following error message during MQtoMSstatsTMTFormat:

** Annotation for Run : CC326, Channel : channel.8 are missed.
** Annotation for Run : CC326, Channel : channel.9 are missed.
........ for all raw files in this Experiment.........
** Annotation for Run : CC333, Channel : channel.8 are missed.
** Annotation for Run : CC333, Channel : channel.9 are missed.
Error in MQtoMSstatsTMTFormat(evidence, proteinGroups, annotation, fraction = T) : 
  ** Please add them to annotation file.

Why would I add these channels to the annotation file? They have not been used and therefore also do not show up in the MaxQuant files.

Any help would be greatly appreciated!

Best regards,
Klemens

messages.author: 0f36a4d38f68e366
messages.subject: Re: MSStatsTMT multiple fractions with differing no. of channels
parts:
Hi Klemens,

Thanks for your interest in MSstatsTMT. Yes, MSstatsTMT can analyze such a dataset.

The MaxQuant evidence files we used usually have the following structures (here only the important columns are listed):


As you seen, each peptide ions (each row) has 10 values from 10 channels of one Raw file (one experiment). So even two channels of your Exp3 are empty, you should still see some values in the corresponding columns. 


My suggestion for your dataset is (1) add the these two empty channels from Exp3 to the annotation file but put "Empty" under their group information; (2)  When doing testing, only compare the two groups primary and recurring tumor. See the reference code:

library(MSstatsTMT)
data(quant.msstats)
Only compare condition 0.125 and 1
levels(quant.msstats$Condition)
#> [1] "0.125" "0.5"   "0.667" "1"     "Norm"
# 'Norm' should be not considered in the contrast
comparison<-matrix(c(-1,0,0,1),nrow=1)
# Set the names of each row
row.names(comparison)<-"1-0.125"
# Set the column names
colnames(comparison)<- c("0.125", "0.5", "0.667", "1")
comparison
#>         0.125 0.5 0.667 1
#> 1-0.125    -1   0     0 1

test.contrast <- groupComparisonTMT(data = quant.msstats, contrast.matrix = comparison)

Best,
Ting

Hi Ting,
Thank you for your support and your response!
"So even two channels of your Exp3 are empty, you should still see some values in the corresponding columns. "

This is only true, if you do a "quick and dirty" analysis in MaxQuant and do not set different group parameters for every experiment (which I did, because I used different channels :) ).
The end result of doing it that way is getting an evidence table, which lacks the columns of empty channels completely. 
I don't know whether you want to consider this or maybe you can put something in your manual / vignette that tells people to always quantify all channels, even if they have not been used. (Or did I miss that?)

To get these "empty" columns I therefore ran a second MQ analysis with all reporter channels for all experiments and included the empty channels in the annotation matrix. +

messages.subject: Re: MSStatsTMT multiple fractions with differing no. of channels
parts:
Hi Klemens,

Thank you very much for sharing the information and your suggestion. I will consider putting explanation in vignettes which tells that MQtoMSstatsTMTFormat() always assume all channels are quantified.

MQtoMSstatsTMTFormat() combines all the fractions (MS runs) from same mixture and puts the mixture value under Run column. So the results you got from MQtoMSstatsTMTFormat seems correct. You can continue the analysis using MSstatsTMT.

Best,
Ting

messages.subject: Re: MSStatsTMT multiple fractions with differing no. of channels
parts:
Hi Klemens,

Cloud you print out "as.character(levels(quant_protein$Condition))".  I guess it has "Norm" as condition, which we shouldn't include as columns of the contrast. See the example

# 'Norm' should be not considered in the contrast 
comparison<-matrix(c(-1,0,0,1),nrow=1) 

# Set the names of each row row.names(comparison)<-"1-0.125"
# Set the column names and 'Norm' should be not considered in the contrast
